::: {.section-hero} This section combines unsupervised machine learning with spatial priority screening to identify recurring urban profiles across Riyadh and examine how those profiles relate to areas of higher greening priority. K-Means clustering is used to discover groups of 500 m grid cells with similar combinations of land surface temperature, vegetation, population, and building coverage. A separate weighted priority score is then used to identify areas where higher heat, lower vegetation, greater population exposure, and stronger built intensity overlap. ::: ::: {.analysis-section} ## Urban Cluster Profiles K-Means clustering grouped the 500 m grid cells into five recurring urban profiles based on four standardized variables: mean land surface temperature, mean NDVI, estimated population, and building coverage. The clustering is unsupervised, meaning the algorithm was not given predefined labels. The resulting groups were interpreted after clustering based on their average characteristics.
**Machine-learning role:** K-Means is the unsupervised machine-learning component of the project. It identifies recurring combinations of urban conditions without assigning greening priority directly.
::: ::: {.analysis-section} ## AI-Assisted Priority Interpretation The AI-assisted analysis examines how strongly each K-Means urban profile is associated with cells classified as **High** or **Very High** greening priority. The strongest associations occur in the **Hot Dense Built-Up** and **Dense Populated Urban** profiles. This provides an additional interpretation layer by showing which recurring urban conditions are most commonly linked with higher intervention priority.
**Important distinction:** this analysis does not replace or recalculate the greening priority score. It uses the K-Means results to interpret how AI-derived urban profiles relate to the independently calculated priority levels.
::: ::: {.map-section} ## Greening Intervention Priority The final greening priority score combines four normalized indicators.
35% Land Surface Temperature
30% Low Vegetation
25% Population Exposure
10% Building Coverage
Higher-priority cells therefore represent locations where hotter surface conditions, limited vegetation, population concentration, and stronger built intensity overlap most strongly.
The priority map is intended as a **spatial screening tool for further evaluation**, not as a direct tree-planting recommendation. Local site conditions, land ownership, infrastructure, water availability, and planning constraints would need to be assessed before any intervention.
:::
